purpose: Map the four unknown classes and their pre-, during-, and post-implementation practices onto the current human-AI collaboration, process-fidelity, hard-standard, Skill-treatment, and capability-governance system without promoting the method to a hard standard or authorizing a new Skill.

quadrants.name: known-knowns
quadrants.risk: explicit facts, goals, constraints, authority, and repository truth are dropped or silently rewritten across hops
requiredResponse: bind explicit facts, target, scope, authority, evidence, and hard standards
preserve source-backed anchors through handoff and transformation
prefer native reasoning or no Skill unless a task-matched method adds measurable value
currentMechanisms: intent intake and repository truth snapshot
quadrants.acceptance: Every predeclared explicit fact remains recoverable and unchanged unless an authorized decision record explains the delta.
quadrants.falsifier: One explicit source fact is omitted, contradicted, or changed without a recorded authorized reason.
quadrants.forbiddenClaim: A successful terminal answer proves lossless intermediate transfer.

quadrants.name: known-unknowns
quadrants.risk: an explicit uncertainty, missing authority, or missing evidence is guessed instead of bounded, asked, researched, or deferred
requiredResponse: record the uncertainty and its decision impact
ask only the highest-impact blocking question or run a bounded authorized check
keep assumptions reversible and visibly separate from facts
optionalMethodCandidates: Matt grill or grill-with-docs when the task and source are bound
Superpowers brainstorming when discovery materially improves the task
quadrants.acceptance: Material explicit unknowns are either resolved with evidence, bounded as assumptions, or left open without being converted into certainty.
quadrants.falsifier: A material known uncertainty becomes an unlabelled fact or unauthorized action.
quadrants.forbiddenClaim: Using an elicitation Skill proves the uncertainty was resolved correctly.

quadrants.name: unknown-knowns
quadrants.risk: tacit user taste, quality judgment, domain experience, or know-it-when-seen criteria remain unexpressed and are replaced by Agent preference
requiredResponse: elicit reactions through small prototypes, variants, references, or concrete contrasts
record confirmed preference separately from speculative inference
retain human creative judgment and consequential choice
optionalMethodCandidates: reviewed external ideation or critique Skill only when task-matched
quadrants.acceptance: A consequential preference is either explicitly confirmed by the user or remains labelled unresolved.
quadrants.falsifier: Silence, one prototype, or one Agent-generated option is treated as confirmed user preference.
quadrants.forbiddenClaim: A plausible prototype proves product preference or user acceptance.

quadrants.name: unknown-unknowns
quadrants.risk: a high-impact hidden constraint, role perspective, codebase interaction, lifecycle edge, or external dependency is never searched for
requiredResponse: run a proportional blind-spot pass before irreversible or high-impact work
inspect relevant roles, code paths, lifecycle edges, official sources, and authorized external evidence
turn discoveries into explicit knowns or known unknowns before action
currentMechanisms: targeted official and reviewed external research
optionalMethodCandidates: task-matched research, review, threat-model, or architecture Skill
independent weak-Agent or reviewer arm after exact dispatch authority
quadrants.acceptance: The blind-spot pass covers predeclared relevant perspectives and any discovered issue is reclassified with evidence and ownership.
quadrants.falsifier: A predeclared high-impact perspective is skipped, or absence of discovery is claimed as proof that no hidden issue exists.
quadrants.forbiddenClaim: A blind-spot scan proves completeness or the absence of unknown unknowns.

lifecycle.artifactPolicy: Use only the smallest durable artifact needed by risk, handoff, and verification.

practices: record material deviations from the plan
bind reason, affected invariant, authority impact, and recovery anchor
reroute at failures, new evidence, or capability-class changes
lifecycle.artifactPolicy: Implementation notes are proportional evidence, not a mandatory universal diary.

practices: explain the delivered result and material tradeoffs
use a quiz or teach-back only when it improves user understanding
run tests, independent acceptance, closure review, and cleanup accounting separately
lifecycle.artifactPolicy: Explanation and quiz evidence cannot substitute for tests, acceptance, authority, or closeout evidence.

scenarioMatrix.hostDifference: transparent and opaque hosts expose different context and compaction evidence
scenarioMatrix.permissionBoundary: read-only binding and accounting; no automatic mutation
scenarioMatrix.metric: predeclared explicit-fact retention and unauthorized-delta count
scenarioMatrix.fallback: stop at the last source-backed anchor and request the missing artifact
scenarioMatrix.falsifiableConclusion: One unaccounted explicit-fact loss rejects process-fidelity acceptance.

scenarioMatrix.hostDifference: question, approval, and research surfaces vary by host
scenarioMatrix.permissionBoundary: no external search, account access, or mutation beyond the bound task
scenarioMatrix.metric: material uncertainty resolution, assumption labelling, and unauthorized-guess count
scenarioMatrix.fallback: keep the uncertainty open and narrow the action
scenarioMatrix.falsifiableConclusion: One material unlabelled guess rejects the method result.

scenarioMatrix.hostDifference: prototype and review modalities differ across CLI, desktop, browser, and domain tools
scenarioMatrix.permissionBoundary: human confirmation remains required for consequential preference
scenarioMatrix.metric: confirmed-versus-inferred preference ratio and correction burden
scenarioMatrix.fallback: retain multiple reversible options and mark preference unresolved
scenarioMatrix.falsifiableConclusion: Treating inference as confirmation rejects preference fidelity.

scenarioMatrix.hostDifference: available code, lifecycle, tool, telemetry, and independent-review surfaces vary
scenarioMatrix.permissionBoundary: discovery is read-only evidence gathering, never action authority
scenarioMatrix.metric: predeclared perspective coverage, discovered-risk reclassification, and false-completeness claims
scenarioMatrix.fallback: narrow the claim and preserve an explicit unknown-unknown residual
scenarioMatrix.falsifiableConclusion: Skipping a predeclared perspective or claiming completeness rejects the scan.

scenarioMatrix.hostDifference: handoff, compression, delegation, tool, review, and cleanup edges vary by host
scenarioMatrix.permissionBoundary: live weak-Agent dispatch requires a separate exact grant and fresh route evidence
scenarioMatrix.metric: new, carried, recovered, unique, peak-active, and first-breach loss plus human review burden
reuseOrder: self-authored treatment only after residual gap
scenarioMatrix.falsifiableConclusion: Terminal correctness cannot rescue an intermediate process-loss failure.

decision.nextBoundedAction: Use the mapping to refine task fixtures and attribution oracles, then compare native, Matt, Superpowers, and existing self-authored phase controls only on named gaps. Keep zero-model fixtures first and require separate exact authority before any weak-Agent dispatch.
